Cluster E from #114 (https://github.com/Xapicc/UsageFoundry/issues/114): *a fleet sharing one account moves in lockstep, because nothing is randomised*. `refusalResumeAt`, `TRANSIENT_BACKOFF_MS` and `sweepPaused`'s single pass are all deterministic and all computed from one coalesced snapshot, so every run computes the same answer and acts on it in the same tick — the budgets sweep reproduced it and got **one** distinct `resume_at` across 25 runs. #114 says one jitter design covers all three, so design it once and apply it consistently.

1. **#102 — An exhausted allowance fails the run unless enforcement is live-resume** — https://github.com/Xapicc/UsageFoundry/issues/102

The default enforcement is `between-cycles` (`settings.ts:326`, `runs/new/page.tsx:169`), so on a shared account meeting the wall terminates runs a park would have preserved.

finalText:
Three commits on `uf/usagefoundry-2-2fda340c`. All three issues were OPEN; none skipped.

## #102 — allowance refusal fails the run unless `live-resume` (`9f9b806`)

The decision came out of `startRun` into a pure `refusalDisposition(...)` beside `refusalResumeAt`, with `refusalKind()` naming the refusal once instead of two inline predicates. **It takes no `enforcement` argument** — there is nothing left to gate on, which is the form the codebase already uses for "an orchestrator block cannot raise its own instance's budget". `MAX_PAUSES_PER_RUN` is unchanged, `evaluateBudget` is untouched (so terminus → cycles → duration → run spend → weekly → session still holds, and `sweepPaused` still ends a parked run on a never-clearing verdict). A run that does spend its waits now says it ran out of *waits*, not that the allowance is gone.

Acceptance: parks under every mode (`refusalDisposition` has no mode); cap and wall clock still bound it (loop `continue` re-enters at the pre-cycle guard — verified at `orchestrator.ts:4482`); 25 runs are now recoverable by `sweepPaused` with nobody opening a page; regression test seen to fail — I temporarily reinstated the `live-resume` gate inside `refusalDisposition` and got `not ok 2 - parks a wall whatever the enforcement mode is` (3 failures), then restored it and got 828/828.

## #103 — jitter the refusal backoff (`c4e9a4c`)

`jitterMs(wait, random, floorMs)` is the one design, shared with #104: uniform over `[0, half the wait]`, floored and capped at 15 min, **never negative** — both callers have a floor underneath them that a shortening spread would undo. `refusalResumeAt` gained an injectable `random`, applied after its own floor and cap and clamped again. The floor on the band is `3 × SWEEP_MS`, because a parked run wakes at the first sweep *after* `resume_at`, so a band narrower than a tick is invisible.

`MAX_RESUMES_PER_SWEEP = 4` is the half no spread reaches — a fleet bunched against `MIN_REFUSAL_WAIT_MS` or carrying a null `resume_at` is due in one tick regardless. Runs over the cap are left exactly as they are (nothing written, so nothing rewritten every 60 s) and reconsidered next tick. Not in `promoteQueued`, which stays the one owner of FIFO order, the folder claim and the cap.

Acceptance: 25 runs one shared boundary, `now` 1 ms apart → ≥24 distinct wakes spanning ≥10 minutes (asserted); the sweeper caps the flip; the reason at the cap names attempts (from #102); jitter injectable, so all six existing `refusalResumeAt` cases keep their original numbers by passing `() => 0`. Seen to fail: with `jitterMs` returning 0 and the resume cap disabled, `not ok 1 - does not wake twenty-five runs at one instant`, `not ok 2 - spreads the backoff rungs too`, `not ok 3 - hands back only so many parked runs per tick` (3 failures) → 832/832 restored.

## #104 — 85 s of unjittered retry (`2c34f81`)

`transientBackoffMs({attempt, kind, random})` replaces the constant lookup. `isRateLimited` is a **strict subset** of `isTransientApiError` (both patterns already match there, asserted in a test), so it widens nothing about what is retried — it selects a ladder and a sentence. `isTransientApiError`/`isUsageLimit` untouched. `RATE_LIMIT_BACKOFF_MS = [30 s, 2 m, 5 m, 10 m]` — 17.5 min at the spread's floor, ~26 min at its ceiling — bounded on the other side by the run's own wall clock, since the retry `continue`s into the pre-cycle guard. `RefusalCause` gained `rate-limited`, whose stop reason names `maxConcurrentRuns` rather than telling the operator to wait.

Acceptance: retry instants spread (25 callers, one attempt index, ≥24 distinct, band ≥40 % of the rung); a sustained 429 tolerates ≥10 min asserted (17.5 actual) rather than 85 s; the two endings have separate causes and sentences; the schedule is pure with an injected source, delays grow *at band edges* (rung n's floor above rung n−1's ceiling — half-width jitter is what buys that), and different randomness at one index gives different delays. Seen to fail: with one shared ladder, a constant lookup and one ending, 7 failures across both new describes → 846/846 restored.

## Verification

```
NODE_ENV=development npm ci --include=dev   # ok
npm run typecheck                           # ok, no output
npm test                                    # 846 tests, 846 pass, 0 fail
grep -n "Math.random\|jitter" src/lib/orchestrator.ts   # hits in both backoff paths (#104's own check)
```

`npm run build` **fails** with `[TypeError: generate is not a function]` — I checked out the base commit `aa42952` and got the identical failure, so it is pre-existing in this container and not caused by this work. Docker is unavailable here, so `docker compose up --build` is unverified; nothing in this change touches the image.

## What #109's author needs to know

`sweepPaused`'s `resume` branch is the only one whose code changed (now gated by `MAX_RESUMES_PER_SWEEP`, decremented on a successful flip). `hold`, `park` and `end` are byte-for-byte unchanged, as is `planPausedRun`'s signature. Two of its *inputs* moved: the set of rows reaching it is wider (#102 parks under every enforcement mode) and the `resume_at` values `duePausedRuns` filters on are now spread (#103).

## #101 and things left alone

**#101 is not on this branch** — `runIteration` still settles only on the child's own `exit`/`close` with no deadline (`orchestrator.ts:3961-3964`). I worked under the assumption that #114's ordering constraint is about deployment risk rather than code dependency, and nothing here needs the deadline to be correct. The consequence stands as #114 states it: parking on a shared wall means more runs holding checkouts for up to `MAX_REFUSAL_WAIT_MS`, and a hung cycle still holds its slot until the container restarts.

Noticed, deliberately untouched: `evaluateBudget`'s own `session_fraction` park is still gated on `live-resume` (explicitly out of scope — that is the operator's configured guard, not the provider's refusal); `pause_count` is still never reset; and a run parked on a refusal that is *already* out of wall clock keeps its folder until its next due sweep rather than being ended at once, because `duePausedRuns` only reconsiders due rows.

One incident to flag: `git stash -u` on a clean tree popped a stash belonging to another worktree into mine. I re-stashed the content immediately — it is `stash@{0}`, labelled `restored: popped into the wrong worktree by usagefoundry-2` — and my tree and commits are intact. The stash list already carried one such note from a previous run, so this appears to be a recurring hazard of shared stash state across these worktrees.

DONE
